title: NY State Assembly · District 78

context.text: Uncontested race. Incumbent George Alvarez advanced from the Democratic and Working Families Party primaries unopposed; no Republican candidate qualified for the general-election ballot.

summary.text: George Alvarez is the unopposed Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent seeking re-election to a third term. Born in the Dominican Republic and a Bronx resident, he sits on the Cities, Codes, Consumer Affairs and Protection, Labor, Real Property Taxation and Transportation committees, and campaigns on affordable housing, public safety, racial justice and economic growth for the Bronx.

background.text: Born in the Dominican Republic; describes himself as growing up in a single-parent, modest-income household.
Earned a bachelor's degree in computer science in the Dominican Republic and a master's degree in logistics in Madrid, Spain, plus a Harvard certification in cybersecurity.
Worked as a Bronx community activist on jobs, housing and social justice issues before serving as a member of Bronx Community Board 1.
A local entrepreneur and job creator prior to his 2022 election to the Assembly.

priorities.text: Quality, affordable housing: says he works to increase accessibility to public housing while decreasing its cost.
Lowering costs and increasing employment for working families struggling with rent, healthcare and food costs.
Public safety: says he is introducing legislation so New Yorkers can live, work and travel with greater peace of mind.

positions.summary: The Assembly’s video page says he joined colleagues, advocates and labor at a March 23, 2026 press conference calling for tax proposals on the ultra-wealthy and most profitable corporations in the final state budget.
positions.quote: calling on the governor to include legislative proposals in the final state budget, making the ultra-wealthy and most profitable corporations pay their fair share of taxes in order to address the affordability crisis.

record.text: Assembly committee assignments for 2025-2026: Cities, Codes, Consumer Affairs and Protection, Labor, Real Property Taxation, and Transportation.
Announced $3 million in capital funding for Keith Plaza and $50,000 for Kelly Tower's senior center in his district.
Introduced the "Bodega Act," legislation intended to boost safety in New York City corner stores, according to his campaign's own account of Bronx Times coverage.

researchNotes: No opposing candidate qualified for the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot in this district. Alvarez has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey; positions and the Bodega Act item rely on his own campaign site rather than an independent news article or bill-text link, since the underlying news article URL and exact bill number could not be independently located.
